proof_summary: For each prime power \(p^i\), counting multiples gives the numerator valuation as \(\sum_{i\ge1}\lfloor m/p^i\rfloor^2\), while Legendre’s formula gives the denominator valuation as \(\sum_{i\ge1} g(\lfloor m/p^i\rfloor)\), where \(g(N)=\sum_{r=1}^N r\lfloor N/r\rfloor\); the bound \(g(N)\le N^2\) also establishes that the quotient is integral. Since \(\lfloor(np+k)/p^i\rfloor=\lfloor np/p^i\rfloor\) for every \(i\ge1\) and \(0\le k<p\), both valuations—and therefore their difference—are constant throughout the block.
